$comment: Recorded pack sizes, refreshed 2026-09-14 and the refresh is the story. `check:artifacts` existed, `artifact-size-ratchet-lock.test.ts` unit-tested its verdict function against synthetic inputs, and **no workflow ever ran the verdict against the real packages** — so seven of them drifted past this file unchallenged: closeout +268%, seniority +112%, paratext +87%, burgee +51%, caique +46%, flagstaff +15%, linegauge +11%. The growth is explained — the PLAN 1.1 schema fold put a 6.5 KB family schema in every package that reaches the plugin registry, and waves 1 and 3 added plugin hosts and drop-in façades — but explaining growth is not the same as accepting it, which is why the numbers are named here rather than quietly replaced. `npm run lint` runs the check now, so the next one is caught. seniority moved 2026-09-20, deliberately and in one direction: 47,616 -> 59,124 gzipped and 153,040 -> 193,682 unpacked, +24.2% and +26.6%. The cause is two drop-in subpaths that did not exist — `seniority/lilconfig` (lilconfig 3.1.3's surface, which took its compat row from 0 / 77 to 67 / 77) and `seniority/rc` (rc 1.2.8's merge without its four dependencies). Both are product, not drift, and the package's own R9 ceiling in `shape.test.ts` — 140,000 B of built `dist`, measured against lilconfig — is still met. The band is raised here rather than the ceiling there, because they measure different things: this one is the tarball a consumer downloads, that one is the graph a bundler walks. **Lowered 2026-09-21, and this direction needs no permission.** `scripts/strip-comments.mjs` read only the top level of `dist/`, so every nested entry point shipped its doc comments: burgee unpacked 949,221 -> 635,640 (-33.0%) and flagstaff 200,204 -> 188,624 the moment it recursed. A ratchet tightening is always free; it is the loosening that is a decision. **2026-09-21: `linegauge` and `seniority` were the two published packages whose build never ran `strip-comments` at all** — not a recursion gap, simply absent from their `build` script. Adding it: linegauge unpacked 83,538 -> 56,148 (-32.8%), seniority 193,682 -> 139,793 (-27.8%). Both directions of this file's history now have the same cause: a stripper that was not reaching what it was supposed to reach. **Raised 2026-09-23, burgee only: 173,668 -> 189,725 gzipped and 677,098 -> 744,915 unpacked (+9.2%, +10.0%).** The cause is the façades' type surface: `burgee/yargs` shipped no `Argv`, `Arguments` or `CommandModule`, so every TypeScript + yargs adoption target failed to compile after `burgee migrate`. `dist/yargs/types.d.ts` is @types/yargs' declarations with their doc comments — 53,093 bytes, the hover text a yargs user already reads — and emits 11 bytes of JavaScript, so no bundle and no import graph moved; the rest is `migrate`'s export table and name check. Declarations keep their comments by the same rule as every other `.d.ts` here (`strip-comments.mjs`). **Raised 2026-09-23, paratext only: 29,566 -> 32,593 gzipped and 92,160 -> 101,438 unpacked (+10.2%, +10.1%).** The cause is A27: `paratext/terminal-link` now carries `supports-hyperlinks` 4.5.0's own detection (`dist/hyperlinks.js`) instead of paratext's `LINK.when`, which disagreed with the incumbent in 30 of 55 environments graded in `hyperlinks.test.ts`. That table is what makes the row level and lets `burgee migrate` rewrite `terminal-link`; the root entry does not import it. **Raised 2026-09-27, closeout only: 31,178 -> 35,140 gzipped and 95,387 -> 109,473 unpacked (+12.7%, +14.8%).** Main already stood at 103,646 unpacked (+8.7%, inside the allowance) from growth since 2026-09-14; this change adds 5,827 B for design R4, which was one third built: `alternateScreen()` and `rawMode()` paired with their undos in the restore phase, the registry finishing the phases a drained event loop left behind, their declarations (doc comments kept, by the `.d.ts` rule above), and the README documenting them. Product, not drift; `weight.test.ts` holds the per-entry budgets and D-163 records the design. **Raised 2026-09-27, linegauge only: 26,717 -> 29,604 gzipped and 83,683 -> 95,160 unpacked (+10.8%, +13.7%).** Main stood at 27,605 / 86,464 just before #655 (+3.3% on both, inside the allowance); #655 adds 1,999 B gzipped and 8,696 B unpacked, and `dist/slice.js` is 7,580 B of it (2,108 -> 9,688): `slice.ts` rewritten over slice-ansi 9.0.1's token grammar and walk, which took `linegauge/slice` from 53 / 104 to 104 / 104, level with the control. The WIDE table generated from get-east-asian-width 1.7.0 (Unicode 17, 122 -> 126 ranges, the 1,147 code points the hand-written one lacked) costs 76 B of `dist/width.js`. Product, not drift; `ceilings.json` holds the per-entry budgets, and #655 moved `linegauge/slice`'s there.caique only: 39,267 -> 62,116 gzipped and 121,782 -> 210,330 unpacked (+58.2%, +72.7%).** The cause is D-152: `caique/clack` was `limitOptions` alone and now carries `@clack/prompts`' twelve prompts, its writers, glyphs and settings on caique's own keypress loop, which is what took clack's graded row from 14 / 17 to 16 / 17. Product, not drift: `./clack`'s static graph is 62,238 B against clack's 101,684 B across six packages (`caique/src/weight.test.ts`), about a third of the unpacked growth is the new `.d.ts` files with their doc comments, and a program that imports caique's own API reaches none of it.
